title: Scotese (2016) PALEOMAP Global Plate Model, from the PALEOMAP PaleoAtlas for GPlates
reference_frame: PALEOMAP (plate 001 'Hot Spot to PMAG' is the identity)
citation: Scotese, C. R., 2016. PALEOMAP PaleoAtlas for GPlates and the PaleoData Plotter Program. PALEOMAP Project. doi:10.5281/zenodo.10251792

license.name: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International
license.statement: The Zenodo record for the PALEOMAP PaleoAtlas for GPlates lists its licence as cc-by-4.0.
license.note: Only the rotation file and the plate polygons are used. The paleogeographic map rasters in the same archive are not unpacked, packed or served: the maps the viewer measures are governed by the separate PALEOMAP website terms, and this project keeps to publishing masks derived from them.

pack.note: About 200 polygons are valid from 0 Ma to 0 Ma. Active only at that instant, they cover nearly the whole globe, so they are dropped when packing.

relationship: Scotese's own rotation model, the lineage behind the published maps this viewer measures, though the maps are the 2002 edition and this model is dated 2016-02-01. Independent of the EarthByte and Torsvik & Cocks models. Its polygons include continental shelves, so its land reaches further than the land segmented from the maps.
limitations: The rotation file states no rule for Palaeozoic longitude; plate 001 'Hot Spot to PMAG' is the identity at every age. Polygons are continental blocks with shelves, not coastlines. Rotations reach 1100 Ma.
